content: Suppressor of fused homolog (SUFU) is a protein in humans that is encoded by the SUFU gene. The SUFU gene encodes a critical component of the sonic hedgehog (SHH) and patched (PTCH) signaling pathway. This pathway plays a pivotal role in normal embryonic development. Mutations in genes that encode components of this pathway can disrupt normal developmental processes and are linked to several cancer-predisposing syndromes. Examples of such syndromes include holoprosencephaly (HPE3), basal cell nevus syndrome (BCNS), and Greig cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome (GCPS). The SUFU protein has been demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including GLI1, GLI3, and PEX26. These interactions are essential for the regulation of the SHH/PTCH signaling pathway and its downstream effects.
